problem: Differentiable planner-adaptation methods (e.g., DiffTune, NeuPAN) rely on static loss functions and gradient-only parameter updates, which get stuck in ineffective parameter regions when execution conditions change. Nothing reuses recovery experience across failures.
motivation: Motion planners tuned under nominal conditions fail under changed conditions such as narrow passages or clutter. Failed adaptation steps carry evidence about why the current optimisation direction fails, and semantic (VLM) feedback can revise objectives, while past recovery experience and cheap simulated rollouts could guide safer, better recovery.
key_idea: Jointly adapt planner parameters and loss weights by alternating auto-differentiation with VLM in-context intervention triggered on stalled adaptation (ILAD), and extend it with memory-retrieved candidate generation, parallel low-fidelity rollout selection and online memory consolidation (MARS).
insight: Gradient updates and VLM reasoning are complementary: in the ablation on 50-obstacle IR-SIM, removing IL drops SR from 94.0 to 74.0 and removing AD drops it to 84.0 with more epochs. In Habitat, the advantage of SERP over w/o MARS grows from -2.3% to 14.6% as memory grows from 50 to 236 entries, showing accumulated recovery memory helps. Note this is a local motion-planner adaptation paper, not a VLN or goal-directed navigation benchmark study.
method: ILAD AD mode: planner parameters θ={q_s,p_u,η,d_min,d_max} are updated by gradient descent on an execution-oriented loss L_ILAD with weights W=(α,β,γ,ω), backpropagated through the differentiable planner (NeuPAN-style MPC).

ILAD trigger: In-context learning is invoked when failure persists over the recent history B_k and the relative loss reduction between first and last loss falls below δ_L; the history is reset afterwards.
ILAD IL mode: a VLM (Qwen3-VL-Plus) reads the failure context (image + outcome) and adaptation history, and jointly revises θ and W, giving a new initialisation for further AD.

MARS memory retrieval: recovery memory M={M+,M-} stores successful and failed traces, indexed by RGB plus two geometric schematics; Qwen3-VL-Embedding-2B retrieves and Qwen3-VL-Reranker-2B reranks by turning angle, clearance and progress.

MARS candidate generation and rollout: the VLM generates J candidate configurations from context, history and retrieved memory; each is evaluated in parallel in a low-fidelity IR-SIM replay of the local failure, with AD updates for up to N rollouts and early stop on success.

MARS selection and consolidation: the VLM picks the best (candidate, rollout step) which is applied in the target environment; the real recovery trace is consolidated into memory (simulated rollouts are not stored).

setting.backbone: Qwen3-VL-Plus (frozen VLM API) for intervention, candidate generation and selection; Qwen3-VL-Embedding-2B and Reranker-2B for retrieval; differentiable NeuPAN-style MPC planner
setting.training_data: none (training-free; online adaptation, memory starts empty and accumulates online)
setting.observation: local perception (lidar / local obstacle geometry), first-person RGB image, reference path, plus geometric schematics
setting.action_space: continuous velocity commands (linear/angular) from an MPC planner for a differential-drive / car-like robot
setting.privileged: reference path (shortest path in original scene) given; recovery is via rollback to a prior feasible state

numbers.eval_set_note: 6 HM3D scenes (00804-00807, 00812, 00813), 50 generated obstacle scenarios each; memory accumulated online
numbers.extra: memory starts empty, online consolidation; low-fidelity rollouts in IR-SIM

numbers_note: Not a standard embodied navigation benchmark; custom IR-SIM and Habitat obstacle scenarios. Habitat SR/collision rates were given as percentages. Real-world results only as success checks and times (Table 4).
results: SERP reaches 95.0/91.0/87.0% success at 30/40/50 obstacles in IR-SIM, versus 79.0/76.0/60.0% for the strongest baseline DiffTune, and cuts collision at 50 obstacles from 35.0% to 5.0%. In Habitat SERP gets 87.7% SR versus 77.0% for DiffTune and 81.3% without MARS. On a real car-like robot it passes an almost-closed door in all 3 configurations, while the baseline fails in all 3.
limitations: Fidelity gap between low-fidelity IR-SIM rollouts and Habitat/real world means selected configs may not recover immediately.
Higher episode time (TotTime 74.72 s vs 49.46 s for DiffTune in Habitat) and reliance on VLM calls (latency) and API models.
Evaluation uses self-built local-planning scenarios with small scale; real-world tests limited to a doorway with few configurations; excludes cases needing global rerouting.
